RAG: retrieve evidence, then generate

For Solutions Architects

Retrieval-Augmented Generation finds relevant private knowledge for each question, places that evidence in the prompt, and asks a language model to answer from it.

    Your role

    Why this matters for a Solutions Architect

    • Separate the offline indexing architecture from the online request path.
    • Place authorization filtering inside retrieval, not only in the user interface.
    • Diagnose retrieval relevance before tuning prompts or replacing the language model.
    • Define citation and abstention behavior as product requirements, not presentation details.

    Quality levers

    • Chunking and metadata determine what can be found.
    • Embedding and reranking determine ordering.
    • Prompt construction and model choice determine synthesis.

    Security boundary

    • Propagate user identity into each retrieval request.
    • Filter source records before they enter model context.
    • Keep citations so access and provenance can be audited.

    Common failure modes

    • No useful chunk: indexing or retrieval problem.
    • Useful chunk omitted from prompt: orchestration problem.
    • Good evidence, wrong synthesis: generation problem.
